domain: Economic History / Technology Studies / Path Dependence Theory
topic_summary: Analysis of QWERTY keyboard layout persistence examining whether its dominance reflects technical necessity (naturalization), path-dependent lock-in with identifiable beneficiaries (manufacturers/incumbents), or rational market selection. The topic tests whether beneficiary-hunting constitutes analytical artifact (D3) or reveals genuine structural extraction.

key_entities: Remington & Sons / Union Typewriter Company (manufacturer, standardization agent)
Telegraph operators (early adopters, transcription priority users)
key_tensions: Technical necessity vs historical accident (jam prevention narrative vs telegraph operator adaptation)
Lock-in inefficiency vs rational persistence (David's market failure vs Liebowitz-Margolis market selection)
Beneficiary extraction vs beneficiary artifact (incumbent protection vs analytical construction)
key_mechanisms: Network effects in typing skill standardization (typists train on employer standard, employers hire trained typists)
Manufacturer consolidation via Union Typewriter Company (1893 merger creating de facto standard)
Navy testing methodology (Dvorak involvement, later methodological critique)
key_absences: Counterfactual evidence: what would alternative-layout adoption have required in 1890s vs 1930s vs 2000s
Quantified switching costs: actual measured cost of retraining vs claimed efficiency gains

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: QWERTY's persistence as either natural/efficient outcome or path-dependent lock-in
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Economic historians and technology scholars interpreting the same historical record

readings.commitment: QWERTY persists because it was/became genuinely adequate; alternatives lapsed through fair competition
readings.authority_grounding: Liebowitz-Margolis empirical historiography; market efficiency presumption
readings.expected_structural_delta: No systematic beneficiary; switching costs reflect genuine skill investment; Dvorak advantage empirically contested

readings.commitment: QWERTY persists through path-dependent coordination failure despite technical inferiority
readings.authority_grounding: Paul David's path dependence framework; network externality theory
readings.expected_structural_delta: Social cost-benefit divergence; no individual beneficiary but collective suboptimality; market failure without extraction

readings.commitment: QWERTY persists because manufacturers/incumbents actively maintained it to protect training investments and market position
readings.authority_grounding: Critical political economy; beneficiary-hunting as analytical method
readings.expected_structural_delta: Identifiable beneficiaries (Remington/Union Typewriter, incumbent typing schools); active suppression of alternatives; extraction via artificial switching costs

axiom_contradictions.basis: Naturalization requires QWERTY to be efficient or efficiency-neutral; lock-in requires it to be inferior to available alternatives. No framework holds both QWERTY-is-adequate and QWERTY-is-inferior simultaneously.

Naturalization denies systematic beneficiaries (outcomes reflect fair competition); beneficiary extraction requires identifiable agents who profit from maintaining the standard. No framework holds both no-beneficiary and beneficiary-extraction simultaneously.

omegas.description: Does the beneficiary_extraction_reading constitute genuine structural analysis or analytical artifact (D3)? If beneficiary-hunting finds beneficiaries by construction, the reading may be methodologically invalid despite narrative coherence. The constraint story generation must test whether identifiable beneficiaries (Union Typewriter, typing schools) demonstrably acted to suppress alternatives vs whether beneficiaries are retrodicted from outcome.
omegas.source: User's explicit D3 ARTIFACT flag; kernel contest framing

omegas.description: What would alternative-layout adoption have required in 1890s (pre-standardization) vs 1930s (Dvorak introduction) vs 2000s (Colemak, software remapping)? Switching cost structure changes across eras; lock-in claims may be era-specific rather than universal.

Liebowitz-Margolis critique of Navy test methodology (Dvorak involvement, bias) vs David's reliance on those tests. If the empirical basis for Dvorak superiority is contested, lock_in_reading's technical inferiority premise weakens. Naturalization and lock-in readings may collapse if Dvorak advantage is artifact.
omegas.source: Switching cost quantification deferred axis; methodological dispute in research context

omegas.description: David's three features (technical interrelatedness, economies of scale, quasi-irreversibility) are theoretical constructs. Were they measured or assumed? If assumed, lock_in_reading may be theoretical projection rather than empirical finding.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (what is treated as background); path dependence theory as lens

omegas.description: How to distinguish genuine beneficiary extraction (agents act to maintain standard) from beneficiary artifact (analysts retrodict beneficiaries from outcome)? Union Typewriter merger (1893) and standardization is observable; active suppression of alternatives is not directly evidenced in research context. Beneficiary_extraction_reading may require evidence of deliberate suppression, not merely outcome-consistent incentives.
omegas.source: D3 artifact concern; beneficiary-hunting methodology critique
